quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: For a face shield to work well, it should NOT:

options.text: Have scratches on it.
Allow you to see to both sides.
Be completely sealed with no air flow.
Fasten tightly to your helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be completely sealed with no air flow.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should have no scratches, let you see to both sides, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. A sealed face shield traps moisture and causes fogging, making it hard to see.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to do only one—either brake or swerve.
Only use the front brake and do not swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions one after the other, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: Hearing protection is:

options.text: Not needed if you wear a helmet.
Needed in addition to wearing a helmet.
Only needed on very windy days.
Not needed if you are carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needed in addition to wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing even with a helmet on. Hearing protection lets you hear important sounds like car horns and sirens while protecting your ears.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Rest stop ahead.
Use high beams.
Turn right.
Danger ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Danger ahead.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, the lead rider extends their right leg to warn others that there is danger on the right side of the road.

questions.question: Riding in cold weather for a long time could cause all of these EXCEPT:

options.text: Tiredness.
Hypothermia (body temperature too low).
Severe chills.
Hot flashes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hot flashes.
questions.explanation: Cold weather riding can cause severe chills, tiredness, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: When riding in traffic and a small animal enters your lane, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes if needed to avoid hitting the animal.
Change lanes as fast as you can.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in your lane when riding in traffic. Swerving into another lane to avoid a small animal can cause you to crash into another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.

questions.question: The right shoes for motorcycle riding should have:

options.text: Long, loose laces.
Short heels.
Tall heels.
Be sneakers only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Short heels.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on the road. Tuck in any laces so they don't get caught on anything.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.
Move your path as needed to handle the curve.
Use the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your path as needed to handle the curve.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or motorcycle with a sidecar turns differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle. You may need to move from the outside of the curve to the inside before straightening out, rather than following the curve exactly.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you want to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you want to go.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: How can you stop other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Move back and forth across your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage car drivers from trying to share your space.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. They tell drivers the rules of the road. You must follow these signs.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before turning.
When turning, lean in the direction you wish to go.
Avoid dragging your feet on the roadway.
Avoid looking at other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid looking at other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Always watch for other traffic on the road. Slow down before turning and lean in the direction you turn. Never drag your feet on the road, as they could catch and cause you to lose control.

questions.question: It is important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: Approaching a police officer.
Someone is following too closely.
There is a stop sign ahead.
Your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Someone is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light if someone is tailgating you. They may not see the hazard that is making you slow down. Also flash your brake light if you are about to slow down where other drivers might not expect it.

questions.question: Because of their small size, motorcycles seem to be:

options.text: Traveling faster than they actually are.
Traveling more slowly than they actually are.
Not moving when they actually are.
Closer than they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traveling faster than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small, so they look like they are going faster than they really are.

questions.question: Which portion of the lane should be avoided?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
No portion of the lane should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No portion of the lane should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best or should always be avoided. Choose your lane position based on the current riding conditions.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly in a curve, you should:

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Abruptly apply both brakes while leaning.
Apply only the rear brake.
Apply only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: First straighten your motorcycle and square the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten, apply the brakes smoothly and slowly. Reduce your lean, then increase brake pressure as you slow.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: First apply the front brake, then the rear.
First apply the rear brake, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes at the same time whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle and trying to turn, you should:

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite of the direction you want to turn.
Not hold the grip because it can be dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle as that can be unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When going faster than walking speed, press the grip in the direction you want to turn. This will make your motorcycle lean the right way to turn.

questions.question: When you are stopped, you:

options.text: Should remain in first gear.
Should remain in neutral.
Should remain in fifth gear.
Can remain in any gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should remain in first gear.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow and stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: Of the crashes involving both a motorcycle and a car, how many are caused by the driver failing to properly yield the right-of-way to the rider?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 25 percent
Over 50 percent
About 90 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: Over 50 percent
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes happen because car drivers fail to yield the right-of-way to motorcycle riders.

questions.question: If your front wheel starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front brake on and ride out the skid.
Keep the front brake on and release the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
Release the front brake and press harder on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up while braking, release the front brake completely right away. Then apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: In normal conditions, how far should you stay behind the vehicle in front of you?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riders do about hearing protection?

options.text: Always wear hearing protection to prevent hearing damage.
Only wear hearing protection on long rides.
Do not wear hearing protection because it blocks out horns and sirens.
Do not wear hearing protection if wearing a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear hearing protection to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage over time, even with a full-face helmet. Earplugs and other hearing protection prevent damage while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: The center of the lane often has an oily strip. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it is wet.
Ride only on the oily strip for better grip.
Avoid the entire center of the lane.
Do not worry about oil or other items in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars builds up in the center of lanes. When the road is dry, this strip usually has enough grip for a motorcycle. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride to either side and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When a vehicle is passing you from behind, where should you position yourself in the lane?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
On the left side of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.
It does not matter where in the lane you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Being too close to the passing vehicle increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: What is the best position in your lane?

options.text: Always the right side.
Always the center.
Always the left side.
It depends on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on road, weather, and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycle brakes is true?

options.text: The front and rear brakes have equal power.
The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
Use only the front brake when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake provides most of the stopping power—at least 70 percent. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, where should you stay in the lane?

options.text: In the center.
On the right side.
On the shoulder.
Use your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center.
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or by an oncoming vehicle, stay in the center of your lane. Riding closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: What protects your eyes from the wind while riding?

options.text: Goggles
Windshield
Sunglasses
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from the wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: Where should less experienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Right behind the leader.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should position themselves toward the front, right behind the leader. This prevents them from having to rush to keep up with the group. More experienced riders behind them can also watch over them.

questions.question: Studies show that nearly ______ of motorcycle riders killed in crashes had been drinking.

options.text: 20 percent
40 percent
60 percent
80 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 40 percent
questions.explanation: Alcohol causes many motorcycle crashes, especially fatal ones. Studies show that about 40 percent of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle:

options.text: Requires a lot of traction.
Requires little traction.
Is a slow maneuver.
Should be done to avoid a hazard on a slippery road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Requires a lot of traction.
questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs a lot of grip on the road to be safe. Do not swerve suddenly on slippery roads.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn both your head and your shoulders to get a better look.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Use only your mirrors.
Only move your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight
How quickly the alcohol was consumed
How often alcohol is consumed

questions.correctAnswerText: How often alcohol is consumed
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. Sex, physical condition, and food intake can also have some effect.

questions.question: To be more visible at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride with your headlight on.
Reduce your space cushion.
Ride in a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on to be seen better at intersections. Ride in a lane position that helps other drivers see you. Keep a safe distance from other vehicles so you can escape if needed. Do not assume a driver sees you just because you made eye contact.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, it is usually best to:

options.text: Increase your speed.
Exit the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane is dangerous when wet. When it rains, follow the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Speed up.
Reduce their speed.
Move their shoulders to match the angle of the turn.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed.
questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down. Release the throttle and use the brakes if needed.

questions.question: When you are being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind, stay in the center of your lane. This makes it harder for the other driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: The effects of marijuana can last for:

options.text: No more than 15 minutes.
About an hour.
About two hours.
More than six hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: More than six hours.
questions.explanation: When smoked, marijuana can affect you within minutes and effects last about two to four hours. When eaten, it takes over an hour to start working, but effects can last more than six hours.

questions.question: When does the motorcycle registration period begin?

options.text: January 1st
February 1st
March 1st
July 1st

questions.correctAnswerText: March 1st
questions.explanation: All motorcycles must be registered with the state and display a license plate. The registration period runs from March 1st through the last day of February.
